headline: Who Really Owns East Maui's Water System?

meeting.body: Who Really Owns East Maui's Water System?
meeting.summary: A presenter questioned whether a private company truly owns the East Maui ditch system, citing old licenses and state land.
meeting.recap: A presenter gave a briefing on the East Maui irrigation system.[[0:00:00]] In 2025, Alexander and Baldwin sold its full interest in the East Maui Irrigation Company.[[0:01:13]] One key ditch section feeds the largest of the county's three East Maui surface water treatment plants.[[0:03:31]] The presenter said the new owner is owned by a Canadian government pension investment board.[[0:04:24]] A state land department letter said the department does not own the system and cannot transfer it.[[0:08:45]] The last water licenses for the four license areas expired between 1971 and 1986.[[0:13:06]] The presenter said those licenses say the aqueducts become government property when the license ends.[[0:13:46]] Last week, state land board staff cited the company's ownership of one ditch section to reject the county's takeover request.[[0:15:16]] No one testified, and testimony closed at 2:12 p.m.[[0:17:13]] The presenter said ownership affects license revenue for the Department of Hawaiian Homelands and the Office of Hawaiian Affairs.[[0:21:41]]

moments.q: "EMI owns the ditch system and has no intention of selling it."
Members begin questions for the presenter
